title: Mexico Proposes Reviewing Foreign Investments over 49% Under National Security Criteria
author: Georgina Saldierna
content:
_This article by[Georgina
Saldierna](https://www.jornada.com.mx/autores/Georgina%20Saldierna) originally
appeared in the [August 30, 2026 edition of La
Jornada](https://www.jornada.com.mx/noticia/2026/08/30/politica/gobierno-
propone-revisar-con-criterio-de-seguridad-nacional-inversiones-foraneas-
mayores-a-49), Mexico's premier left wing daily newspaper._

The Executive sent the Congress's Permanent Commission an initiative to reform
the Foreign Investment Law, which will **subject the approval of foreign
capital exceeding 49 percent in Mexican companies to a national security
criterion**. To allow that evaluation, the bill proposes strengthening the
National Foreign Investment Commission by **incorporating the heads of the
Secretariats of National Defense, Navy, and Security and Citizen Protection**
, as well as of the Attorney General's Office, the National Intelligence
Center, the Tax Administration Service, and the Financial Intelligence Unit of
the Secretariat of Finance.

That body will have to review the acquisitions that foreign capital seeks to
make for a percentage greater than 49 percent in the energy, transport,
health, communications, mining, data processing and storage, digital systems,
aerospace, and defense sectors and sensitive facilities, as well as in
critical technologies such as artificial intelligence, robotics, and
semiconductors, among others.

The reform states that the inclusion of those authorities is indispensable to
prevent foreign acquisitions of Mexican companies that put national security
at risk.

If the Mexican company transmits, cedes, hands over, or transfers the
shareholding to the investor despite having received the Commission's denial
of authorization for the acquisition, it will be **fined between 586,000 pesos
and 23,062,000 pesos**.

The president of the Permanent Commission and of the Senate, Laura Itzel
Castillo, said that the presidential proposal was referred to this chamber.
